newsitem.title: FRANCE: ALPINE SKIING-VAL D'ISERE MEN'S DOWNHILL POSTPONED.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-VAL D'ISERE MEN'S DOWNHILL POSTPONED.

text.p: Heavy fog forced World Cup organisers to call off a men's downhill on Saturday after 17 of the 72 racers had skied the course.
The race was postponed until Sunday with a super-giant slalom scheduled for that day put back until Monday.
Austrian Josef Strobl was leading when the downhill was halted, with a time of one minute 56.79 seconds, with Frenchman Adrien Duvillard lying second.
But under World Cup rules, two-thirds of the starters must race before a result can be declared valid and so the standings were wiped out.

The start of the race, which would have been the season's first downhill after a race in Whistler, Canada, last week was called off because of heavy snow, had been put back two-and-a-half hours because of poor visibility on the OK piste on Saturday morning.

Seventeen racers completed the 3.4-km course but steadily worsening fog in the middle section slowed them down and forced organisers to call a halt just before defending World Cup champion Luc Alphand of France was due to start.
After a 45-minute-break the fog remained and racing was called off for the day, much to the relief of the skiers.

"It's unacceptable to have skiers go down in these conditions," said world champion Patrick Ortlieb of Austria, who had set the fastest time in practice but clocked only 1:58.00 from start position 13 in the race.
Heavy snowfalls had forced organisers to cancel one practice run and a women's giant slalom on Friday.
Last year, the Val d'Isere classic downhill had to be run in two legs after poor visibility made it impossible to start from the top of the piste.
Organisers said the downhill would begin at 0930 GMT on Sunday, when sunny weather is forecast. The super-G was rescheduled for 1100 GMT on Monday.

A men's slalom is scheduled for Madonna di Campiglio, Italy, on Tuesday and World Cup sources said organisers were considering providing helicopters to transport the racers to the Dolomite resort after Monday's super-G.
